slack_list_channels.rationale: Lists Slack workspace channels: `List public or pre-defined channels in the workspace with pagination`. Because this reaches workspace data using the user's/server's Slack credentials, channel listings may be non-public or account-specific, so SECRET. Channel names/topics/purposes can be created or edited by workspace participants; the description says `public or pre-defined channels in the workspace`, so the returned channel metadata is multi-writer Slack content and UNTRUSTED. The exact returned fields are not advertised, so output-field classifications are undetermined; least restrictive reading keeps labels.

slack_post_message.rationale: Posts agent-supplied content to Slack: `Post a new message to a Slack channel`. This is a WRITE and a SINK because `channel_id` selects the Slack channel destination and `text` is sent/stored there; Slack channel messages may be read by other workspace members. No returned data is specified.

slack_reply_to_thread.rationale: Sends agent-supplied content into a Slack thread: `Reply to a specific message thread in Slack`. This is a WRITE and SINK because `channel_id` and `thread_ts` select the channel/thread destination, and `text` is the reply content sent/stored for Slack readers. No returned data is specified.

slack_add_reaction.rationale: Changes Slack state by adding an emoji to a selected message: `Add a reaction emoji to a message`. It is a WRITE and SINK because `channel_id` and `timestamp` decide which Slack message is acted on, and `reaction` is the value being sent/stored as the reaction name, visible to Slack readers. No returned data is specified.

slack_get_channel_history.rationale: Retrieves Slack messages: `Get recent messages from a channel`. Messages in the user's workspace/channel can be non-public SaaS data reached with Slack credentials, so SECRET. Channel messages are authored by other workspace users and may contain attacker-controlled/injected content in a multi-writer source, so UNTRUSTED. `channel_id` decides the channel read. Returned message bodies and related user/timestamp identifiers are not enumerated by the advertised schema, so field classifications are undetermined; least restrictive reading keeps labels.

slack_get_thread_replies.rationale: Retrieves Slack thread messages: `Get all replies in a message thread`. Thread replies in Slack may be private/account workspace data reached with credentials, so SECRET. Replies are authored by other Slack users in a multi-writer source, so they are UNTRUSTED. `channel_id` and `thread_ts` decide the thread read. Returned fields are not specified, so output-field classifications are undetermined; least restrictive reading keeps labels.

slack_get_users.rationale: Retrieves Slack workspace users and profiles: `Get a list of all users in the workspace with their basic profile information`. Workspace membership/profile information is SaaS data reached with credentials and may be non-public, so SECRET. Basic profile information such as names/profile fields can be set by workspace users, making it attacker-controllable in a multi-user workspace and UNTRUSTED. Returned fields are not specified in the tool schema, so field classifications are undetermined; least restrictive reading keeps labels.

slack_get_user_profile.rationale: Retrieves detailed Slack profile data: `Get detailed profile information for a specific user`. Detailed profile information is SaaS/account workspace data reached with credentials and may be non-public, so SECRET. Profile fields can be authored by the user whose profile is fetched, an outside workspace participant relative to the current user, so UNTRUSTED. `user_id` decides which user's record is read. Returned fields are not advertised, so output-field classifications are undetermined; least restrictive reading keeps labels.
